title: primitive-module-api-and-upgrade-plan
content:
Summary:
This doc sketches the intended public interface for the primitive Terraform modules we maintain for Private Deployments (VPC, IAM, EKS/GKE/AKS). It combines opinionated API decisions, recommended variables/outputs, and an upgrade/migration strategy for breaking changes. Goal is to minimize churn for customers using the modules in Dedicated/Private installs while enabling improvements (defaults, better security, multi-AZ defaults).

Context and constraints:
- These modules target two classes: (A) cloud-managed private deployments (VPC + managed k8s: EKS/GKE/AKS) and (B) air-gapped on-prem packaging where we still expose a compatible inputs/outputs surface (some inputs ignored on-prem).
- We aim for stable semver for module interfaces: patch=no breaking changes, minor=additive, major=breaking requiring migration plan.
- Avoid exposing sensitive values in outputs (kubeconfig should be base64 + marked sensitive in Terraform configuration).

Design principles (short):
- Minimal required inputs: make sensible defaults for CIDRs, naming, tags.
- Explicit resource ownership: modules should accept an optional prefix/owner tag instead of implicitly concatenating org ids.
- Idempotent, deterministic names: use format <env>-<team>-<resource> with configurable separator.
- Keep outputs small and interoperable with other modules: prefer maps of ids over many separate outputs when possible.

Module interface sketches:
1) Module: ri-vpc (primitive)
- Purpose: create VPC, subnets (public/private), nat gateways (optional), route tables, and required route associations.
- Variables (recommended minimal set):
  - name_prefix (string, default="ri")
  - environment (string, default="dev")
  - cidr (string, default="10.0.0.0/16")
  - az_count (number, default=2)
  - private_subnet_suffixes (list(string), default=["private-a","private-b"])
  - public_subnet_suffixes (list(string), default=["public-a","public-b"])
  - enable_nat (bool, default=true)
  - nat_single_az (bool, default=false) // for cost-constrained installs
  - enable_flow_logs (bool, default=true)
  - flow_logs_destination (string, default="") // support for logging bucket or cloudwatch
  - tags (map(string), default={})
- Outputs (recommended):
  - vpc_id (string)
  - private_subnets (list(string))
  - public_subnets (list(string))
  - azs (list(string))
  - route_table_ids (list(string))
  - nat_gateway_ids (list(string))
  - default_security_group_id (string)
  - metadata (map(string)) // small map for convenience: {name_prefix, environment}
- Notes: prefer returning lists in AZ order. Keep number of outputs moderate so dependent modules can reference lists directly. Avoid outputting CIDR block details unless requested via optional outputs flag.

2) Module: ri-iam (primitive)
- Purpose: centralize IAM role and policy creation patterns used by private deployments (eks node role, controller roles, cross-account roles for logging/backups).
- Variables (recommended):
  - name_prefix (string)
  - environment (string)
  - create_eks_node_role (bool, default=true)
  - extra_role_definitions (list(object)) // NOTE: we don't model this deeply in the primitive; see compose module for complex policies
  - tags (map(string), default={})
- Outputs (recommended):
  - eks_node_role_arn (string)
  - eks_node_role_name (string)
  - role_arns (list(string)) // for any extra roles created
- Notes: avoid embedding policy JSON in module variables for maintainability; accept references to managed policy ARNs or a path to a maintained policy resource.

3) Module: ri-k8s-cluster (primitive)
- Purpose: create managed k8s cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS) or provide a shim that wires into an existing cluster. Provide kubeconfig as sensitive output.
- Variables (recommended):
  - provider (string enum ["eks","gke","aks","external"]) default="eks"
  - cluster_name (string, default="${name_prefix}-${environment}-cluster")
  - vpc_id (string)
  - private_subnet_ids (list(string))
  - public_subnet_ids (list(string))
  - control_plane_version (string, default="latest-compatible")
  - node_groups (list(object)) // minimal spec: {name, instance_type, desired_capacity, min,max}
  - enable_oidc (bool, default=true)
  - endpoint_public_access (bool, default=false) // default: private endpoint only for private deployments
  - kubernetes_network_plugin (string, default="aws-vpc-cni")
  - addons (list(string), default=["vpc-cni","coredns","kube-proxy"]) // cluster add-ons
  - tags (map(string))
- Outputs (recommended):
  - cluster_id (string)
  - cluster_name (string)
  - kubeconfig (string) // mark sensitive in module usage
  - cluster_endpoint (string)
  - cluster_ca_cert (string)
  - node_group_ids (list(string))
  - oidc_provider_arn (string) // conditional
- Notes: keep provider abstraction thin. For cross-cloud compatibility, document which inputs are ignored or required per provider. Offer example compose module that wires ri-vpc + ri-iam + ri-k8s-cluster.

Variables vs locals guidance:
- Keep variables small and explicit; use locals inside modules to compose names and defaults.
- Avoid using data lookups at apply-time that may vary unpredictably (e.g., query latest AMI without pinning). If needed, expose pinned_ami_map variable.

Outputs guidance:
- Always include a metadata output on each primitive with {name, uid, created_at} (UID can be deterministic hash) so higher-level code can reconcile resource ownership during upgrades.
- Do not expose credentials or secrets. For kubeconfig, return base64-encoded string and mark as sensitive.

Compatibility and upgrade strategy (high level):
1) Versioning policy:
  - Modules live in the registry with semver tags. Use >= provider constraints in example usage but not in module itself where possible.
  - Deprecate by creating a migration doc and a warning output in the module to surface at plan-time (terraform 0.13+ "warning" via null_resource local-exec echo during plan is hacky; prefer docs and PR notices).

2) Backwards-compatible changes (minor):
  - Add optional variable with a default, add outputs, internal refactor that doesn't change resource addresses.
  - Add flags to toggle new behavior (e.g., enable_flow_logs_v2) defaulting to false.

3) Breaking changes (major):
  - Changing resource address schema (name templates) or output types requires major bump. Provide automated migration helper (small CLI script or terraform state mv snippets) in the module repo under /scripts/migrate-0.X-to-1.0.sh.
  - Provide a transition module (compatibility shim) that maps old outputs to new outputs for a 1-2 release window.

3) State migration playbook (for infra owners):
  - Step 0: create a migration branch and add thorough unit/integration test.
  - Step 1: run terraform plan with new module pinned in a non-prod workspace and capture diff.
  - Step 2: if resource addresses changed, run terraform state mv commands documented in scripts/ to map old to new.
  - Step 3: apply with terraform apply in canary region/namespace (or non-production account) to validate behavior.
  - Step 4: roll out across remaining environments with a puppet-like controlled schedule.

Canary rollout pattern for module updates:
- Use a compose module (ri-private-deploy) that consumes primitives pinned at versions. Update primitives in the compose to new version and deploy to a single dev workspace first. Verify: networking, kube auth, node registration, logging.
- If cluster-level change, create a temporary node pool that uses new configuration, cordon/drain older nodes via k8s orchestration, then decommission. Avoid in-place control plane re-creation unless absolutely necessary.

Testing and CI recommendations:
- Unit: terratest or kitchen-terraform unit tests for simple cases.
- Integration: full apply in sandbox AWS account with cleanup; run smoke tests: cluster API responsive, nodes ready, sample pod scheduled on each AZ.
- Pre-merge: run a checklist script that lints HCL, validates variables documentation, and runs terraform fmt & validate.

Operational considerations & best-practices:
- Defaults: multi-AZ (>=2) by default; let small installs opt down via explicit flags.
- IP management: document how to change CIDR safely; prefer allocating extra CIDR range via shared IPAM if available.
- Logging: enable flow logs by default but allow disabling for extremely cost-sensitive installs.
- Tags: default required tags: {owner, environment, cost_center} and expose tags input to extend.
- Secrets: integrate with KMS/HSM for disk encryption and avoid secrets in tfstate by using remote state + workspace encryption.

Example quick interface snippets (usage):
- Compose module (ri-private-deploy) minimal example (pseudo):
  module "vpc" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//ri-vpc"
    name_prefix = "redwood"
    environment = var.environment
    cidr = "10.20.0.0/16"
  }
  module "iam" {
    source = "./ri-iam"
    name_prefix = module.vpc.metadata.name_prefix
  }
  module "cluster" {
    source = "./ri-k8s-cluster"
    provider = "eks"
    cluster_name = "${var.environment}-cluster"
    vpc_id = module.vpc.vpc_id
    private_subnet_ids = module.vpc.private_subnets
  }

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical metadata UID algorithm (simple sha1 of resource ARNs + prefix?)
- How to best surface deprecation warnings at plan time in a Terraform-native way? Research provider hooks or pre-apply checks.
- Compose module: should it enforce a single module registry version for all primitives or allow each primitive independent pinning? (tradeoff: predictable parity vs easier incremental upgrades)
- On-prem: define minimal shim to accept an existing network plugin and skip VPC creation while maintaining outputs compatibility.

Migration notes from earlier modules (lessons learned):
- Previous breaking change: renamed subnet outputs in ri-vpc -> caused widespread state mv operations; mitigation: provide compatibility module that re-exports old output names for one release period.
- Always include scripts/ state-mapping examples in PR that proposes a breaking change.

Appendix: quick variable/output tables (human readable)
- ri-vpc variables: name_prefix, environment, cidr, az_count, private_subnet_suffixes, public_subnet_suffixes, enable_nat, enable_flow_logs, flow_logs_destination, tags
- ri-vpc outputs: vpc_id, private_subnets, public_subnets, azs, route_table_ids, nat_gateway_ids, default_security_group_id, metadata
- ri-iam variables: name_prefix, environment, create_eks_node_role, extra_role_definitions, tags
- ri-iam outputs: eks_node_role_arn, eks_node_role_name, role_arns
- ri-k8s-cluster variables: provider, cluster_name, vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, control_plane_version, node_groups, enable_oidc, endpoint_public_access, kubernetes_network_plugin, addons, tags
- ri-k8s-cluster outputs: cluster_id, cluster_name, kubeconfig, cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert, node_group_ids, oidc_provider_arn

Contacts / next steps:
- Owners: Aisha Patel (primary), Marco Chen (vpc/infra), Sofia Martinez (k8s/ci)
- Action items:
  - [Aisha] write compatibility shim prototype for old subnet outputs (due 2025-02-25)
  - [Marco] prototype migration scripts for state mv (due 2025-03-05)
  - [Sofia] add terratest cases for multi-AZ apply (due 2025-03-12)

Notes-to-self / scratch:
- Keep examples minimal in README; add full examples under examples/ for EKS, GKE, AKS, and external-k8s.
- Consider a small CLI that wraps recommended terraform state mv commands for common rename patterns.
- Slack thread: #infra-private-deployments has context: message 16234 about previous breakage.

End.
